title: Exploring AI models in games - writeup
author: NotPornAccount
selftext:
I've been experimenting with running small models (1B \~1Gb) as the main feature of a game. They are somewhat playable but take a lot of testing/refining to get working properly.

For context - one game is Art Dev Tycoon with the Janus Pro model. Janus is around 1B parameters, it can create images and also analyse images. The game loop is about creating art, getting it critiqued, selling it. Game progression is about getting experience with different mediums which levels-up the prompts behind the scenes which means you can create better art works.

Stuff I've tried:

All projects have a test-prompt-suite where I run batches of prompts trying stuff out to see what works reliably/consistently. So I would generate batches of 50-100 where I'll usually go through the outputs, quickly mark outputs with tags, then see what the data says about the tags.

What I found with was

\- the type of model matters (diffusion vs sequential) Janus is a pixel-by-pixel generator. So When I was trying to generate simple images (apple on white background) Janus would get trapped into making everything white. SD Turbo (a slightly larger diffusion model) would have blurry backgrounds

\- they are really good at some things (cats/dogs/faces) but terrible at things they don't know. However they do have a very broad base. So if you ask for a cat that's sleeping - bad output. However you can ask it for rare animals and it generally knows them.

\- instead of one giant prompt, do smaller individual prompts. Janus marks it with a system a bit like 'does it have good colours?' -> Yes.... Does it have good.... -> Sort of

\- I was able to scale the quality of the output. Level 1 pencil is simple child-like drawing, Level 7 is akin to masterful artwork with a dynamic background.

\- It has a crappy procedurally generated fallback that could be used to game the system. I think it's important to have a backup but you should make sure the game can't be abused without it.

Anyone else doing this? What are you building?

I'm stopping dev for this and moving on to a different AI-model-based game, but if anyone's interested it's at [Github - MichaelTJ/ArtDevTycoon](https://github.com/MichaelTJ/ArtDevTycoon) playable at [Art Dev Tycoon](https://michaeltj.github.io/ArtDevTycoon/). I've left the dev options available so you can play around.
